clauses.text:
By the authority vested in me as President and as Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, the following Executive Orders are 
amended as follows:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Amendments to Executive Order 9158. Executive Order 9158 
of May 11, 1942 (Air Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9242–A 
of September 11, 1942 (Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 
1942, to Provide that the Air Medal May Be Awarded to Persons Serving 
with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United States), 
is further amended as follows:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) The first paragraph is amended—

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) by striking ‘‘Army and Navy’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Armed 
Forces’’;

clauses.label: (ii)
clauses.text:
(ii) by striking ‘‘any person’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘those individ-
uals’’;

clauses.label: (iii)
clauses.text: (iii) by inserting ‘‘Air Force, Space Force,’’ after ‘‘Marine Corps,’’; and

clauses.label: (iv)
clauses.text:
(iv) by striking ‘‘distinguishes, or has distinguished, himself’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘distinguish, or have distinguished, themselves’’.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (b) The second paragraph is amended—

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) by amending the first sentence to read as follows: ‘‘The Air Medal 
and appurtenances thereto shall be of appropriate design approved by 
the Secretary of Defense and, under such regulations as the Secretaries 
of the military departments may prescribe, may be awarded by the Secretary 
of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, 
or the Secretary of Homeland Security with respect to the Coast Guard 
when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, or by such commanding 
officers of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, or 
Coast Guard as the said Secretaries may respectively designate.’’; and

clauses.label: (ii)
clauses.text:
(ii) in the second sentence, by striking ‘‘his jurisdiction’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘the jurisdiction of the Navy’’.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The following new paragraph is added at the end of the Executive 
Order: ‘‘The regulations of the Secretaries of the military departments con-
cerned with respect to the award of the Air Medal shall, so far as practicable, 
be uniform and shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense.’’.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Amendments to Executive Order 8809. Executive Order 8809 of 
June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 
of March 31, 1943 (Amendment of Executive Order No. 8809 of June 28, 
1941, Establishing the Good Conduct Medal), and Executive Order 10444 
of April 10, 1953 (Amendment of Executive Order No. 8809 of June 28, 
1941, Establishing the Good Conduct Medal, As Amended by Executive 
Order No. 9323 of March 31, 1943), is further amended—

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) by striking ‘‘men’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘members’’;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) by inserting ‘‘and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of 
the United States Space Force,’’ after ‘‘August 27, 1940,’’;

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) by inserting ‘‘and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of 
the United States Space Force,’’ after ‘‘December 7, 1941,’’; and

Executive Order 14085 of October 3, 2022 
Expanding Eligibility for Certain Military Decorations and 
Awards 
By the authority vested in me as President and as Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, the following Executive Orders are 
amended as follows: 
Section 1. Amendments to Executive Order 9158. Executive Order 9158 
of May 11, 1942 (Air Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9242–A 
of September 11, 1942 (Amending Executive Order No. 9158 of May 11, 
1942, to Provide that the Air Medal May Be Awarded to Persons Serving 
with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United States), 
is further amended as follows: 
(a) The first paragraph is amended— 
(i) by striking ‘‘Army and Navy’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Armed 
Forces’’; 
(ii) by striking ‘‘any person’’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘those individ-
uals’’; 
(iii) by inserting ‘‘Air Force, Space Force,’’ after ‘‘Marine Corps,’’; and 
(iv) by striking ‘‘distinguishes, or has distinguished, himself’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘distinguish, or have distinguished, themselves’’. 
(b) The second paragraph is amended— 
(i) by amending the first sentence to read as follows: ‘‘The Air Medal 
and appurtenances thereto shall be of appropriate design approved by 
the Secretary of Defense and, under such regulations as the Secretaries 
of the military departments may prescribe, may be awarded by the Secretary 
of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, the Secretary of the Air Force, 
or the Secretary of Homeland Security with respect to the Coast Guard 
when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, or by such commanding 
officers of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, or 
Coast Guard as the said Secretaries may respectively designate.’’; and 
(ii) in the second sentence, by striking ‘‘his jurisdiction’’ and inserting 
in lieu thereof ‘‘the jurisdiction of the Navy’’. 
(c) The following new paragraph is added at the end of the Executive 
Order: ‘‘The regulations of the Secretaries of the military departments con-
cerned with respect to the award of the Air Medal shall, so far as practicable, 
be uniform and shall be subject to the approval of the Secretary of Defense.’’. 
Sec. 2. Amendments to Executive Order 8809. Executive Order 8809 of 
June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 
of March 31, 1943 (Amendment of Executive Order No. 8809 of June 28, 
1941, Establishing the Good Conduct Medal), and Executive Order 10444

1941, Establishing the Good Conduct Medal, As Amended by Executive 
Order No. 9323 of March 31, 1943), is further amended—

(b) by inserting ‘‘and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of 
the United States Space Force,’’ after ‘‘August 27, 1940,’’; 
(c) by inserting ‘‘and on or after December 20, 2019, in the case of 
the United States Space Force,’’ after ‘‘December 7, 1941,’’; and

to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency,

employees, or agents, or any other person.

versions.research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 14085 (signed 2022-10-03; 87 FR 60541; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14085.txt, read in full) amends six earlier orders on military decorations and awards (EO 9158 Air Medal, EO 8809 Good Conduct Medal, EO 10694 unit citations, EO 11046 Bronze Star Medal, EO 13830 delegation of authority to approve decorations, EO 11545 Defense Distinguished Service Medal) to cover the Space Force and to use gender-neutral and updated wording, and adds general provisions. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory fragmented the sections, so I replaced it with eight clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition. Later instruments: a search of held order texts for the number 14085 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy; the dossier chain lists no event, and the ofr_catalog search records no disposition note naming it. Current law: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints each amended order with a status line naming EO 14085: EO 9158 as amended by section 1, EO 8809 by section 2, EO 10694 by section 3, EO 11046 by section 4, EO 13830 by section 5 (notes under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57) and EO 11545 by section 6 (note under 10 U.S.C. 1125) (jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv, USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl); the amended orders are therefore printed as current text with the amendments embodied. One caution is stated plainly: the Code's editorial note under 10 U.S.C. 7276 records that section 4(a) of EO 14085 (substituting Homeland Security for Transportation in paragraph 1 of EO 11046) could not be executed because EO 13286 had already made the identical amendment; section 4(b) to (d) are not affected by that note, and the clause for section 4 is claimed operative on the strength of those paragraphs and the printed amended text, not on 4(a). The order cites no statute as its authority (the Constitution and the laws generally, and the President's office as Commander in Chief); the Code sections the amended orders refer to are not held and I assert nothing about them. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes; none carries a coverage warning and none records a revocation or supersession of EO 14085.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No clause has an own-terms end. No held order, statute text or search result amends, revokes or supersedes EO 14085, and the Code prints all six amended orders with the amendments embodied; the only note on non-execution concerns section 4(a), which duplicated an earlier amendment, and is addressed in the section 4 clause.","independent_command_check":"Each of sections 1 to 6 amends one separate earlier order and is independent of the others; section 7 is a separate set of general provisions. The Code prints each amended order as current, so none was found ended.","savings_check":"The order has no savings or transition clause beyond section 7(a), which preserves agency authority and OMB functions. No ending is claimed, so no residual consequence needs separate treatment.","scope_check":"The corrected inventory has eight clauses covering the whole order: the recital and lead-in, sections 1 to 6 and section 7."}
